title: Configuring Settings for the Traffic Capture Policy

blocks.text: With Zscaler Traffic Capture for Network Detection and Response (NDR), you can capture traffic as PCAPNG files with the Traffic Capture policy. Before configuring the Traffic Capture policy, you must enable Traffic Capture and configure a cloud storage destination.

When configuring a cloud storage destination for Traffic Capture, the Zscaler service requires the storage container to have the proper permissions. Certain permissions are only necessary when testing the connection between the Zscaler service and the cloud storage container; these permissions should be removed after the connection has been tested and established. The following table lists the necessary container permissions for testing the connection and subsequent uploading of capture data:

table: Blob write and read data actions

blocks.text: To configure the settings for the Traffic Capture policy:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Traffic Capture > Settings.
On the Traffic Capture tab, click Settings.
In the Settings drawer:
Status: Select to enable Traffic Capture for NDR.
Obfuscate: Choose to obfuscate information in Traffic Capture policy data:
Users: Choose whether the names of users in created PCAPNG files are Visible or Obfuscated.
Devices: Choose whether device information in created PCAPNG files is Visible or Obfuscated.
Click Save.
See image.
In the Cloud Destinations section, click Add Destination, and select one of the following:
AWS S3 Storage: If AWS S3 is your chosen cloud destination, provide the following information in the Add AWS S3 Storage drawer:
Storage Name: Enter a name for your cloud storage destination.
AWS Access ID: Enter the ID associated with your organization's S3 bucket.
AWS Secret Key: Enter the password associated with your organization's S3 bucket.
S3 Folder URL: Enter the URL associated with your organization's S3 bucket.

The Zscaler service does not support custom or directory-style bucket URLs that include non-standard prefixes, additional subdomains (e.g., s3express), or unconventional naming patterns (such as double dashes). You must use a general purpose S3 bucket URL following the standard format: https://<bucket-name>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<path>.
See image.
Azure Storage: If Azure is your chosen cloud destination, provide the following information in the Add Azure Storage drawer:
Storage Name: Enter a name for your cloud storage destination.
Account Name: Enter the name of your Azure storage account.
Storage Name: Enter the name of your configured Azure Blob storage container.
Tenant ID: Enter the Tenant ID associated with your organization's Azure cloud storage destination.
Client ID: Enter the Client ID associated with your organization's Azure cloud storage destination.
Client Secret: Enter the Client Secret associated with your organization's Azure cloud storage destination.
See image.
Select Use Default Storage to set the cloud storage destination as the default for your organization.
Click Test Connection and Save to verify and save the cloud destination configuration, then activate the change.
